'''Sir John Stranger Holman''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRSC|CChem}} (born 16 September 1946)<ref name=who/> is an English chemist and academic. He is emeritus professor of chemistry at the [[University of York]], senior advisor in education at the [[Gatsby Foundation]], founding director of the National STEM Learning Centre,<ref name=YorkUni>{{cite web|title=Professor Sir John Holman|url=http://www.york.ac.uk/chemistry/staff/academic/emeritus/jholman/|website=University of York|access-date=20 January 2015}}</ref> Chair of the Bridge Group, past president of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] (RSC),<ref name="RSC2016">{{cite web|url=http://www.rsc.org/news-events/features/2016/jul/new-president-2016//|title=Presidential plans|date=16 July 2016|access-date=22 November 2016}}</ref> and of [[The Association for Science Education]] (ASE).<ref name="ASE">{{cite web|url=https://www.ase.org.uk/|title=Association for Science Education|website=ase.org.uk}}</ref>
==Education==
Holman was educated at the [[Royal Grammar School, Guildford]], and [[Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge]], where he was awarded a [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree with Honours in 1967.<ref name=who>{{Who's Who | author=Anon| title=Holman, Sir John (Stranger) | id = U250632 | year = 2017 | doi =10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.U250632 | edition = online [[Oxford University Press]]|location=Oxford}}</ref>

==Career==
Holman served as a Headteacher of [[Watford Grammar School for Boys]] between 1994 and 2000,<ref name=who/><ref>{{cite web |title=John Holman – Biography |publisher=[[Department for Children, Schools and Families]] |url=http://www.dcsf.gov.uk/stem/biog.shtml |access-date=1 January 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090415052621/http://www.dcsf.gov.uk/stem/biog.shtml |archive-date=15 April 2009}}</ref> and was the British government's National STEM Director from 2006 to 2010<ref name="RS-Holman">{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/john-holman/|title=Sir John Holman|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|access-date=27 April 2015}}</ref><ref name="BBCNews2009">{{cite news|title=Honour for top science educator|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/science/nature/8435305.stm|website=bbc.co.uk|date=31 December 2009 |publisher=[[BBC News]]|access-date=20 January 2015}}</ref> (STEM referring to the academic disciplines of [[Science, technology, engineering, and mathematics]]). He served as president of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] from 2016 to 2018,<ref name="RSCcouncil">{{cite web|title=Our structure|url=http://www.rsc.org/about-us/our-structure/#council|website=rsc.org|publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry|access-date=20 January 2015}}</ref> and was a trustee of the [[Natural History Museum, London|Natural History Museum]] (2011–2019).  He was the founding director of Salters' Advanced Chemistry programme,<ref name="UoY">{{cite web |title=Professor Sir John Holman |url=http://www.york.ac.uk/chemistry/staff/academic/emeritus/jholman/ |access-date=27 April 2015 |website=york.ac.uk |publisher=[[University of York]]}}</ref> and is the author of numerous chemistry textbooks.

Holman is author of the ''Good Career Guidance'' report for the Gatsby Foundation,<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.gatsby.org.uk/education/focus-areas/good-career-guidance | title=Good Career Guidance &#124; Education &#124; Gatsby }}</ref> which is the basis for the English government's national strategy for career guidance in schools: ''Careers strategy: making the most of everyone's skills and talents''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/careers-strategy-making-the-most-of-everyones-skills-and-talents|title=Careers strategy: making the most of everyone's skills and talents|website=gov.uk}}</ref>  He is independent strategic adviser on careers guidance to ministers in the Department for Education. (2021 - ) Holman also authored the ''Good Practical Science'' report<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gatsby.org.uk/education/programmes/support-for-practical-science-in-schools |title=Good Practical Science |website=gatsby.org.uk|year=2017}}</ref>  and was the lead author of Improving Secondary Science guidance report for the Educational Environment Foundation (2018).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://educationendowmentfoundation.org.uk/|title=Education Endowment Foundation|website=educationendowmentfoundation.org.uk}}</ref> He is a member of the Wolfson Foundation's School Panel. (2020)

===Awards and honours===
Holman was [[Knight Bachelor|Knighted]] in the [[2010 New Year Honours]].<ref name=who/><ref name="BBCNews2009" /> In 2014 the Royal Society of Chemistry awarded him the [[Lord Lewis Prize]] "in recognition of his extensive influence over [[chemistry education]] policy".<ref name="LewisPrize">{{cite web|title=Lord Lewis Prize 2014 Winner|url=http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/LordLewisPrize/2014-Winner.asp|website=rsc.org|publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry|access-date=20 January 2015}}</ref> Holman was named in 2014 by the [[Science Council]] as one of the UK's 100 leading practising scientists,<ref name="SC100">{{cite web|url=http://www.sciencecouncil.org/content/100-leading-uk-practising-scientists|website=sciencecouncil.org|title=100 leading UK practising scientists|publisher=[[Science Council]]|access-date=27 April 2015|archive-date=16 January 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140116095841/http://www.sciencecouncil.org/content/100-leading-uk-practising-scientists|url-status=dead}}</ref> and was the 2014 recipient of the Royal Society's biennial [[Kavli Education Medal]], "in recognition of his significant impact on science education within the UK".<ref name="Kavli">{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/awards/kavli-education-medal/|website=royalsociety.org|title=Kavli Education Medal|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|access-date=27 April 2015}}</ref> He was elected President of the [[Yorkshire Philosophical Society]] in 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ypsyork.org/resources/articles/a-new-president-for-the-yps-2018/ |author1=Smith, Carole |title=A new President for the YPS, 2018 |publisher=Yorkshire Philosophical Society |accessdate=4 May 2021}}</ref>
